problem: Portal V2 visual models expose rich data, but chart marks can still require interpretation before a user knows what a point means or how to act on it.
rootCause: Meaningful SVG marks use local title and focus semantics, while explanation and action handoff live at surface level. Without one semantic-selection contract, touch users and keyboard users cannot consistently pin a datapoint and retain its context.
root_cause: Meaningful SVG marks use local title and focus semantics, while explanation and action handoff live at surface level. Without one semantic-selection contract, touch users and keyboard users cannot consistently pin a datapoint and retain its context.
preventionRule: Every meaningful portal visual datapoint must support tap/click and keyboard selection, persistent selected context, an explanation path and an action path without inventing source data.
prevention: Derive semantic labels only from existing title, aria-label or visible text.
Make primary datapoint selection work without hover.
Persist the selected point until another point is chosen.
Keep direct Context and Action handoffs next to the selected meaning.

evaluation.expected: Semantic labels prefer explicit visual meaning, remain bounded, and visual points keep one consistent select-understand-act interaction contract.
